company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 expected), but the quality was low — the upside was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point gross margin tailwind) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105 basis point tailwind), not organic strength. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1% expectation, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal signals a strategic push deeper into the robotics and AI perception space.

MillerKnoll posted solid FQ1 EPS upside (53 cents vs. 36 cents expected), and notably would have beaten even excluding the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (42 cents adjusted vs. 36 cents expected). Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The appointment brings greater leadership stability to the finance function.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents expected) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the 13.85% consensus, despite revenue coming in slightly above estimates at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflationary pressures, and rising material costs as headwinds, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without offering formal guidance yet. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, which demonstrated 22% weight loss in the trial. The strong efficacy data positions VK2735 as a competitive entrant in the high-growth obesity drug market. The results are a significant catalyst for the stock and the broader GLP-1 sector.

sectors: RV industry faces macro headwinds per THOR Industries — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets and retail demand. GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a positive read-through from Viking's VK2735 weight loss data. Robotics and Physical AI space highlighted by Cognex's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings and news note for Tuesday, September 22nd. No broad macro or Fed commentary in today's note, so let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth fiscal quarter earnings — fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street's fifty-four dollars and three cents — but don't get too excited about the quality. The upside was driven by tariff refunds, which provided a 145 basis point gross margin tailwind, and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is less impressive. Domestic comps came in at just plus one-point-six percent versus the plus three-point-one percent the Street was looking for, and operating expenses as a percent of sales rose 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note that sales improved in the final eight weeks of the quarter versus the first eight, and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Overall this is a mixed print — beat on the headline, but the underlying drivers were not organic.

Next, Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly five hundred million dollars upfront, plus an additional one hundred and six-and-a-half million. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million dollars in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a strategic move deeper into robotics and AI, and the growth profile of the acquired business is impressive.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid earnings beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected — and importantly, even excluding the eleven-cent tariff refund benefit, they still would have beaten at forty-two cents. Sales missed, down three-point-three percent organically, but orders rose three-and-a-half percent year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed slightly, but EPS guidance was left unchanged. A mixed but generally respectable quarter.

THOR Industries missed on earnings — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected. Gross margins collapsed 230 basis points year-over-year to twelve-point-four percent, far below the nearly fourteen percent the Street modeled. Management flagged stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation as ongoing headwinds. The company expects a flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 and won't give formal guidance until later in the fall. There were some positives — dealer inventories are healthy and the North American towable RV order backlog surged about seventy-five percent year-over-year — but the headline read is weak.

Finally, Viking Therapeutics is the name to watch this morning. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 obesity drug, showing twenty-two percent weight loss. That is a strong efficacy readout and puts Viking firmly in the conversation as a competitive player in the obesity drug market. Expect read-through reactions across the GLP-1 space.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the high-momentum story, AutoZone is a low-quality beat to watch carefully, and THOR gives us a cautious data point on the consumer discretionary and macro-sensitive RV market. Stay focused and trade the setups.
